docs.summary: SCID-X1 is a genetic disorder of blood cells caused by DNA changes in a gene that is required for the normal development of the human immune system. The purpose of this study is to determine if a new method, called lentiviral gene transfer, can be used to treat SCID-X1. This method involves transferring a normal copy of the common gamma chain gene into the participant's bone marrow stem cells. docs.title: Pazopanib Hydrochloride in Treating Patients With Metastatic Kidney Cancer Who Have No Evidence of Disease After Surgery
conditions: Stage IV Renal Cell Cancer AJCC v7
docs.summary: This randomized phase III trial studies how well pazopanib hydrochloride works compared to placebo in treating patients with kidney cancer that has spread to other parts of the body and have no evidence of disease after surgery. Pazopanib hydrochloride may stop the growth of tumor cells by blocking some of the enzymes needed for cell growth and by blocking blood flow to the tumor.

docs.title: Improving Pain Management and Long Term Outcomes Following High Energy Orthopedic Trauma (Pain Study)
docs.summary:
The purpose of this study is to definitively resolve questions regarding the use of multimodal pharmacologic pain management for orthopedic trauma patients in the context of a multicenter, randomized clinical trial.

Also, as a significant proportion of this population develops chronic post traumatic osteoarthritis (PTOA), a sub-objective of this study is to examine the etiology and incidence of chronic pain and PTOA in this population.

docs.title: Blinatumomab in Treating Younger Patients With Relapsed B-cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
docs.summary: This randomized phase III trial studies how well blinatumomab works compared with standard combination chemotherapy in treating patients with B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia that has returned after a period of improvement (relapsed). Immunotherapy with blinatumomab may allow the body's immune system to attack and destroy some types of leukemia cells. It is not yet known whether blinatumomab is more effective than standard combination chemotherapy in treating relapsed B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

docs.title: Study of Pembrolizumab (MK-3475) vs Placebo for Participants With Non-small Cell Lung Cancer After Resection With or Without Standard Adjuvant Therapy (MK-3475-091/KEYNOTE-091)

docs.title: A Study of Tirzepatide (LY3298176) in Participants With Obesity or Overweight

* the recommended dose for Phase 2

docs.title: Trial to Evaluate ALN-CIDEB in Adults With Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD)
docs.summary:

docs.title: A Phase 1/2a Study of K-1728 in Advanced Solid Tumors
docs.summary: This first-in-human, open-label, multicenter study evaluates K-1728 administered as monotherapy and in combination in participants with advanced or metastatic solid tumors. The study assesses the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and preliminary antitumor activity of K-1728.

docs.title: Oral VK2735 for Weight Management Phase 3 (SUNRISE 1)
docs.summary: This study is one of two planned Phase 3 studies to support the weight management indication for VK2735 Oral in obese (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2) or overweight (BMI ≥ 27kg/m2) adults with at least one weight-related comorbidity without type 2 diabetes mellitus.

docs.title: Oral VK2735 for Weight Management in Adults With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus Phase 3 (SUNRISE 2)
docs.summary: This study is one of two planned Phase 3 studies to support the weight management indication for VK2735 Oral in obese (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m2) or overweight (BMI ≥ 27 kg/m2) adults with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.

docs.title: A Study of EloraTZP in Adult Participants With Obesity Without Type 2 Diabetes
docs.summary:
The purpose of this study is to investigate the efficacy and safety of eloralintide and tirzepatide coformulation (EloraTZP) compared with tirzepatide, eloralintide and placebo for body weight reduction in participants with obesity.

Participation in the study will last about 2 years.

docs.summary: The main purpose of this study is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of eloralintide compared with a placebo in participants with obesity or overweight, type 2 diabetes, and increased cardiovascular risk.

docs.title: Prognostic Value of Oxygen-15 Water PET in Coronary Artery Disease
docs.summary: This study evaluates the prognostic value of quantitative myocardial perfusion imaging using oxygen-15 water positron emission tomography in patients with clinically suspected or known coronary artery disease (main basket), and explores temporal changes in myocardial perfusion related to disease progression, underlying pathophysiological processes, or treatment-related effects (additional baskets).

docs.title: A Study of IPG11406 Tablets in Participants With Lupus Nephritis
docs.summary:
Lupus Nephritis (LN) is one of the most serious and common complications of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). It is a chronic inflammatory disease triggered by abnormal autoimmunity and the deposition of immune complexes in the kidneys. Approximately 40% to 60% of SLE patients develop lupus nephritis at the onset of the disease, and the cumulative rate of kidney involvement during the course of the disease can even reach 90%.

docs.title: KC1086 in Combination With Fulvestrant for HR-Positive, HER2-Negative Advanced Breast Cancer
conditions: HR-positive, HER2-negative Locally Advanced or Metastatic Breast Cancer
docs.summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetic characteristics of KC1086 in combination with fulvestrant in adults with hormone receptor-positive (HR+), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative (HER2-) locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer.

docs.title: A Study to Assess the Effect of Pacibekitug on Major Cardiovascular Events in Patients After a Myocardial Infarction
docs.summary: The main purpose of this study is to demonstrate the superiority of pacibekitug compared to placebo in reducing the risk of 3-point coronary major adverse cardiovascular events (3P-Coronary- MACE), defined as a composite of coronary heart disease (CHD) death, non-fatal myocardial infarction (MI), and urgent coronary revascularization, in participants after an MI, at high cardiovascular (CV) risk and receiving standard of care (SoC) secondary CV prevention therapies.

docs.title: A Research Study of a New Medicine NNC0662-3168 for Weight Management and Type 2 Diabetes
docs.summary: The purpose of this study is to learn more about NNC0662-3168 as a potential treatment for people living with overweight or obesity and/or type 2 diabetes(T2D). The study will investigate its safety, tolerability and its effects in the body. The study will be conducted in four parts. Part A: Single Ascending Dose, Part B: Multiple Ascending Dose: Part C: Dose-finding in Weight Management. Part D: T2D proof-of-concept.

docs.title: A Study to Investigate the Efficacy and Safety of Dato-DXd-based Combinations in Participants With TROP2 NMR+ NSCLC
docs.summary: Phase II, open-label, multicentre, multi-cohort platform study to determine the efficacy and safety of Datopotamab Deruxtecan (Dato-DXd)-based combinations for the treatment of TROP2 NMR+ NSCLC.

docs.title: Delayed Application of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors in Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
conditions: Metastatic NSCLC - Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
docs.summary: This study is a multicenter, randomized, open-label phase 3 trial of delayed administration of immunotherapy in patients who are planned to receive chemoimmunotherapy for newly diagnosed, advanced or metastatic, PD-L1 positive NSCLC without sensitizing alterations in EGFR, ALK, or ROS1.

docs.title: Fighting Osteoporosis With Risedronate Co-Therapy During Incretin
docs.summary: Tirzepatide produces rapid, clinically meaningful weight loss. In older adults, however, substantial weight reduction may accelerate loss of bone and muscle, increase frailty risk, and compound age-related skeletal vulnerability. The purpose of this study is to find out if taking risedronate along with tirzepatide preserves musculoskeletal health during tirzepatide-associated weight loss.
